page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head centred at the top, page number at the top right. Signature mark at the foot.

main_text.p: nim: Quod est in sublimi sol oriens Domini, hoc est bonę fœminę pulchritudo in eius domus ornamento. Sicut enim sol in meridie dū ab exortu iam peruenit ad altissima, hoc est, ad lineam meridianam, vel circulum, per polos & cenith capitis transeuntem, mundū illuminat: sic virtuosa mulier illuminat domum suam: & eius honestissima species, habitudo & praesentia, domum & domesticos suos perornat, clarificat & gubernat. Sicut turpis & improba confundit totam suam p-geniem.

Quæ vero sit honesta & bona mulier, videntur Apostoli exponere, 1. Tim. 2.1. Pet. 3. nempe quæ in amictu modesto cum verecundia & castitate ornat semetipsam, non tortis crinibus, aut auro, aut margaritis, aut vestitu sumptuoso, sed quod decet mulieres profitentem pietatem per bona opera. Quæ enim bona est, benefacit, bonumque operatur, tum erga omnes, tum vero maxime erga familiares, & domesticos fidei, Galat. 6.1. Timot. 5. sicuti decet filias Sarae.

Quinta est constantia & perseuerantia in bonitate & virtutibus praedictis: vt non ter-reatur mulier vllo timore, sed occultus, qui est in corde homo, careat omni corruptela, quemadmodum Petrus docet. Sic enim hic legimus: Lucerna splendens in sacro cande-labro, est formae venustas in aetate constan-ti.i. formosa mulier quae proba manet. page.notes: Long s and u/v/i/j were normalised as instructed. "p-geniem" is a line-end hyphenated word ("progeniem") and the abbreviation mark before "geniem" is unclear, so it is only partly read. "1. Tim. 2.1. Pet. 3." is copied as printed; the chapter and verse numbers are hard to separate at this resolution. "praedictis" is a likely reading of a worn word. The catchword is absent: the page ends on the hyphenated "con-".
